subject: No-train / derivative exclusion - procurement & ops path
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@healthcore.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@healthcore.com
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data-use commitments for pilot - no-training + evidence timeline

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and our security team reviewed Redwood's standard DPA and have two urgent asks before we can present to legal: a firm no-training / no-model-improvement commitment for tenant data (we need contract language and an operational proof path), and a list of subprocessors plus evidence that tenant data will not be used for model updates.

Specific asks and timeline:
- Contract amendment: can you provide a short DPA addendum that states HealthCore tenant inputs and outputs will not be used to improve models (no-derivative, no-train) and defines permissible telemetry?
- Evidence pack: we need an ops checklist and one-week sprint to deliver evidence (logs, KV handling, KMS config) by 2027-03-28.
- Subprocessors: canonical list and any planned changes in next 90 days.
- SLA / credits: security has asked whether making this commitment triggers any SLA or credit exceptions for the hosted plan.

Can you confirm you can meet the 3/28 evidence deadline and share a proposed redline? If dedicated or private deployment is required to meet our assurance bar, flag that as well.

Best,
Alex Morgan
Senior Procurement Manager
HealthCore Therapeutics

--
HealthCore prefers attachments in PDFs; I can push internal approvals quickly if we get clear language and ops steps.

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@healthcore.com>
Cc: david.kim@redwoodinference.com, kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data-use commitments for pilot - no-training + evidence timeline

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. We can meet the evidence deadline; below is a pragmatic path and three contract options depending on how prescriptive you want the controls to be. Attached: No-Learn-Implementation-Outline.pdf and a draft redline for the DPA (DPA_HC_redline_v1.pdf).

Quick path:
1) Contract language: we can supply a single-sentence operative commitment for hosted API customers: "Redwood will not use Customer-provided inputs or generated outputs from the HealthCore account to train, improve, or adapt any model used to serve Customer requests." Couple of definitional clauses for telemetry and aggregated metrics follow in the addendum.

2) Operational evidence (deliverable by 2027-03-28):
   - Ops checklist (attached) covering: request routing, KV cache eviction policy, ephemeral prompt retention, telemetry sampling, and KMS key scoping.
   - Subprocessor inventory export (we'll provide current list + planned changes cadence).
   - Short internal runbook showing how we enforce no-training on hosted capacity (prefix caching disabled for opt-out, sampling thresholds).

3) Deployment options (trade-offs):
   - Hosted API + opt-out flag: fastest for pilot, our runtime supports per-tenant no-learn flags. Lower isolation than Dedicated; operational proofs are the primary mitigant.
   - Dedicated capacity with no-learn enforced at instance-level: stronger isolation, predictable throughput, monthly reserved contract required.
   - Private deployment (VPC/on-prem): full control for HealthCore but longer lead time and procurement route.

4) SLA / credits: committing to no-training does not automatically change our published SLOs, but for Dedicated/Private deployments we can discuss custom SLAs and credit remedies. For hosted with opt-out, we can provide an operational attestation; credits would be considered for material SLA exceptions tied specifically to the no-learn controls.

Next steps I propose:
- Legal: review redline attached; Kimberly, can you look at the DPA addendum and confirm any language we should tighten?
- Ops: David, can you confirm the evidence checklist and whether we have a runnable export of the current subprocessor list?

If that all looks good Alex, we'll get the evidence pack to you by EOD 3/28.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Head of Product, Privacy & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: No-Learn-Implementation-Outline.pdf, DPA_HC_redline_v1.pdf

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com, alex.morgan@healthcore.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 08:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data-use commitments for pilot - no-training + evidence timeline

Alex / team — quick technical notes to support the evidence pack and the addendum language. Below is the operational proof outline I will deliver by 3/28.

Operational proofs we will provide:
- Subprocessor inventory export: CSV with current list (storage provider, metrics provider, telemetry pipeline). We'll timestamp and hash the export for audit.
- KMS scoping: screenshot + export showing HealthCore tenant key (when on Dedicated/Private) or tenant-scoped key IDs for hosted opt-out.
- KV/prefix policy: hosted opt-out sets KV retention to ephemeral (TTL <= 5 minutes) and disables prefix caching for the tenant. Evidence: runtime config snapshot and recent logs showing eviction events.
- Telemetry sanitization: sampling rules and PII filters applied before metrics aggregation; sample config and sanitized logs (scrubbed).
- No-train enforcement: internal flagging system that prevents model update pipelines from ingesting any data tagged with HealthCore tenant ID; we'll provide a screenshot of the pipeline gating and a short recording of a gating check.

Attachment: ops-evidence-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet mapping each evidence item to an ops owner and delivery ETA).

On subprocessors: the current list includes our infra provider (third-party GPU infra), a metrics vendor, and a CI/CD provider. No immediate subprocessor changes are planned in the next 90 days; if anything changes we commit to 30-day notification for enterprise customers. We'll include that in the addendum.

Kimberly — legal redline comments would be helpful on the proposed "no-training" sentence around the scope of "outputs" (do we want to enumerate system-generated metadata vs. user content?).

-David
David Kim
Director, Production Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@healthcore.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@healthcore.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data-use commitments for pilot - no-training + evidence timeline

Soojin / David / Kimberly — thanks for the rapid follow-ups and the attachments so far. A few quick clarifying points from security:

- We'd like the addendum to explicitly state that outputs generated by the model for HealthCore requests are "customer outputs" and will not be used for training, including derivative datasets created for benchmarking.
- For hosted opt-out, we need the ops checklist to include the exact runtime config key names we can audit (so we can validate the opt-out flag during acceptance testing).
- Regarding subprocessors, please include a one-line assurance that any metrics vendor receives only aggregated, non-identifiable metrics for HealthCore tenants.

If you can incorporate those items into the 3/28 evidence pack we'll fast-track legal review. On the SLA question — procurement would like to know if dedicated capacity is a hard requirement for no-train enforcement or whether hosted with opt-out + attestation is acceptable for a pilot. If hosted is acceptable we'd prefer to avoid the procurement delay.

I'll review the redline and come back with a few legal edits if necessary. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Alex
Senior Procurement Manager
HealthCore Therapeutics
